claims: C1 models should obey developer instructions
C2 an instruction from the developer level is overridden by a root instruction that conflicts with it
C3 an instruction from the developer level is overridden by a system instruction that conflicts with it
C4 the obligation to obey a developer instruction does not apply when that instruction is overridden by a root or system instruction

concepts.name: developer_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction given by a developer using the OpenAI API, carrying developer-level authority

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: root_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction at the root level of authority
concepts.inference: the clause says developer instructions are overridden by root or system instructions, so there must be root-level and system-level instructions to do the overriding

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction at the system level of authority
concepts.inference: the clause says developer instructions are overridden by root or system instructions, so there must be root-level and system-level instructions to do the overriding

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is at authority level L
concepts.inference: the hierarchy ranks levels, so each instruction must be assigned a level for the comparison to work

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: instruction I1 and instruction I2 direct incompatible behavior in the same situation
concepts.inference: 'overridden' means the higher-level instruction prevails in a conflict, so a conflict relation between instructions is needed

ontology.inference: the clause speaks of root and system instructions as the overriding kinds, so these classes must exist
ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the root level of authority

ontology.inference: the clause speaks of root and system instructions as the overriding kinds, so these classes must exist
ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the system level of authority

obeying developer instruction % is forbidden when it is overridden by root or system instruction %

closure.reason: the clause obliges obedience to developer instructions and forbids it only when overridden by a root or system instruction; an instruction that is not overridden remains permitted to obey, so silence permits
